idRule: id = <client>-<TAG>-<YYYY>-<MM>-<seq>. TAG names the account (CHQ chequing, USD US-dollar chequing, BCD business card, PCD personal card, BRK brokerage). YYYY-MM is the month of the row date. seq is the 1-based position of the row among that account and month, in file order (header lines do not count). Rows missing from an export get the next numbers of their month.
amountConvention: amount is the cash effect on the company account: money in is positive, money out is negative. On a card a charge is negative and a payment positive (the card CSV shows the opposite sign). post lines list the coded entry: dr and cr in dollars, the last line is the bank or card account itself.
postingCurrency: CAD: every post line, adjusting entry and trial balance figure is in Canadian dollars; USD rows are posted at the monthly test rate in fx

flags.rule: financed tractor: class 16 addition with interest and principal
flags.detail: Used tractor bought 2 Jun 2025 for $118,000.00 plus $15,340.00 HST. Only $33,340.00 left the chequing account; $100,000.00 was financed by Lakeview Equipment Finance (Test) at 8.5% over 60 months with no bank row. Class 16 addition $118,000.00; HST claimed as an input tax credit (June is a refund month). Nine payments from July: split each into interest and principal using the onboarding table; do not expense the whole payment.
flags.action: flag for a person; do not decide alone

flags.rule: personal costs on the business card: groceries and a family flight
flags.detail: Nine grocery charges (about $1,140.00) and a family flight ($1,642.00) are on the business card. Coded to amounts due from the shareholder (1300) until a person decides between shareholder loan, taxable benefit or pay. Not business expenses; no input tax credit.
flags.action: flag for a person; do not decide alone

flags.rule: CRA instalments do not agree: bank shows four, CRA credits three
flags.detail: The bank shows four instalments of $3,500.00 (30 Jun, 30 Sep, 31 Dec 2025 and 31 Mar 2026), $14,000.00 in all. CRA's record (onboarding) credits three; the 31 Dec 2025 payment is not credited. A person asks the client and CRA to move the credit before instalments are entered on the return.
flags.action: flag for a person; do not decide alone

flags.rule: non-deductible penalty on a late HST return
flags.detail: CRA charged $412.37 in August 2025 as penalty and interest on a late HST return. Penalty is not deductible: added back on Schedule 1 (the interest part on the same payment: a person confirms). Not an ordinary expense.
flags.action: flag for a person; do not decide alone

flags.rule: one customer only: worker status and personal services business signs
flags.detail: All revenue is weekly settlements from Transcan Freight Ltd. (Test), one carrier. The owner drives the tractor. A person looks at whether the arrangement looks like employment (personal services business signs) and whether the company has its own equipment, insurance and risk. The tractor and insurance point to a real business.
flags.action: flag for a person; do not decide alone

flags.detail: The year runs 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026. The T2 is due six months after year end (30 Sep 2026); the calendar-year figures a client quotes (T-slips, CRA letters) straddle two fiscal years; instalments fall on 30 Jun, 30 Sep, 31 Dec and 31 Mar.
flags.action: flag for a person; do not decide alone

flags.rule: HST payable at year end: March 2026 return (monthly filer)
flags.detail: The March 2026 return is due 30 Apr 2026, after year end; the adjusted trial balance shows $265.46 owing (account 2050).
flags.action: flag for a person; do not decide alone
